newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Trade in Banespa remains suspended.
newsitem.headline: Trade in Banespa remains suspended.

text.p: Trade in shares of troubled Brazilian state bank Banespa remained halted on the Sao Paulo bolsa despite word the suspension may be lifted in the afternoon, officials said.
"It remains suspended and we don't know if it will be resumed later this afternoon," a bolsa spokeswoman said.

Trade in Sao Paulo state-owned Banespa was suspended Tuesday after a newspaper reported the bank posted a 786.3 million-real, nine-month net profit and the bolsa and Brazil's Securities and Exchange Commission (CVM) asked for more information.
A bolsa official had said in the morning that trade was authorized to resume in Banespa after midday.
The spokeswoman said she did not know why the suspension was not lifted.

Meanwhile, shortly before noon, Sao Paulo state signed a debt restructuring deal that transfers Banespa, whose preferred share is among those making up the bolsa's 49-share Bovespa index, to the federal government.
Banespa preferred had risen some 160 percent in the eight sessions before its suspension Tuesday on speculation over a deal with the federal government to restructure the state's debt to the bank.
